recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-16316 unless FHIR-I reopens the broader transactional-integrity policy in a future issue.
issue_request: FHIR-16316 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for STU3 asking the HTTP Transactional Integrity section to mention PATCH as a way to mitigate some create/update integrity problems, especially distinguishing intentional blanking from client ignorance of fields.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites svn revision 14171. In git, commit 014cb13a38a7133c35b917260bc476d925810439 (GF#16316) added the PATCH paragraph to source/http.html under Transactional Integrity. Later edits preserved the substance while normalizing wording from PATCH operation to PATCH interaction.
additional_context: source/http.html is the current RESTful API (HTTP) narrative page, linked from source/documentation.html. Later same-section work, including FHIR-24914 and FHIR-40957, added nearby returned-resource guidance and terminology cleanup without reversing or narrowing the FHIR-16316 statement. Confluence FHIR-I minutes for 2018-07-09 list FHIR-16316 in the persuasive block vote, and bounded Zulip/Confluence searches found only tracker or commit notifications plus supporting minutes, with no conflicting later decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/http.html already says the PATCH interaction offers support for changing part of a resource and should be used when a client wishes to change just part of a resource, while still warning that transactional integrity issues remain important.
